purpose: Independent synthetic reference inputs for the approved T10, T11, T15 and T16 acceptance scenarios.
scope: Test data only. Not a legally approved calendar, risk methodology, clinical validation or authority submission.

provenance.method: Expected values fixed independently of application code; calendar weekdays, included working days and descriptive arithmetic cross-checked in SQLite. PSUR cutoff and numerator-provenance examples explicitly distinguish the observation window, knowledge cutoff and freeze timestamp.

calendarProfile.holidayScope: Only the expressly listed holiday is used in these examples; this is not a complete production calendar.
calendarProfile.legalDateMeaning: End of the specified local date; this maximum does not displace the duty to act without undue delay.
calendarProfile.safetyDateMeaning: Internal SafetyDue must not be later than the raw calendar target and may be earlier.
calendarProfile.jurisdictionRestriction: EU reference only; do not infer GB rules from these examples.

deadlineCases.reason: Moving Sunday only to Monday still leaves one included working day; the minimum-two-working-days rule also applies.
Calendar-day calculation crosses the Dublin spring DST transition; adding a fixed number of elapsed hours is not equivalent.
January 1 is explicitly a holiday in this synthetic profile; January 4 and 5 are the two included working days.

awarenessInvariant.reason: Late system intake does not replace the preserved first organizational awareness event.

descriptiveRateReference.metric: Observed synthetic events per 10000 device-years, not a causal or clinical-risk estimate.
descriptiveRateReference.reason: Event counts rise while the exposure-normalized descriptive rate falls; raw count growth alone does not establish a rate increase or statistical significance.

psurGeographyReference.reason: Worldwide already includes the geographical subset; adding both aggregates double-counts. If both tables are published in a subset report, all eight counted case versions must remain traceable, including the three outside the subset.

psurCutoffReference.reason: For this explicitly declared period-end knowledge cutoff, both numerator and baseline case evidence must use the same one case. Later knowledge may only enter a separately identified update/supplement, not silently change the baseline numerator while remaining absent from its source set. A freeze timestamp is not itself proof of historical state at the cutoff.

psurHistoricalNumeratorReference.precondition: A matching approved exposure exists for N and N2; this is a complete deliberately constructed synthetic one-case input, not a claim of clinical data completeness.
psurHistoricalNumeratorReference.reason: A closed older case need not be presented as an open N carry-over, but its exact case version/hash must still be frozen as a source for the N2 event count. Numerator provenance must not be limited to current-period narrative cases.
